summary: All 10 TDD Anchor cases are present and meaningfully implemented; tests exercise real AES-GCM operations rather than mocks, every assertion ties to observable behavior (plaintext equality, AEADBadTagException root cause, IllegalStateException message containing the property name). The boot-validation test correctly asserts ApplicationContextRunner failure with the descriptive IllegalStateException for blank / non-hex / wrong-length keys plus a positive happy-path bean assertion, satisfying the tech-spec criterion. One bonus test (decryptRejectsNonTwelveByteIv) covers the explicit decrypt-side IV-length guard called out in the task's Edge cases. No critical or major issues. A handful of minor gaps remain: NUL-byte plaintext is not exercised (spec lists it as a worth-testing edge case), the decrypt IV check is not asserted on the null branch, and the boot test relies on substring matching on stack-trace text (works, but brittle to a future class rename).

findings.title: NUL-byte plaintext round-trip not asserted
findings.description: The task's Edge cases section explicitly calls out 'Plaintext containing NUL bytes — UTF-8 preserves them; round-trip should work.' as a behavior that should be confirmed, and the spec's Testing Strategy bullet for TokenEncryptor says round-trip works 'for ASCII and Unicode payloads' which is silent on embedded NULs. Currently no test passes a plaintext with an embedded '\u0000' through encrypt/decrypt, so a future regression in the UTF-8 boundary (for example, accidentally using a C-style string truncation utility on the plaintext path) would not be caught.
findings.suggestion: Add a small test, e.g. `roundTripWithEmbeddedNulBytes`, that encrypts the string "bot\u0000token\u0000end" and asserts the decrypted output equals the original byte-for-byte. One assertion, no new fixtures, exercises the same code path as roundTripUnicode but pins the NUL edge case.

findings.title: decryptRejectsNonTwelveByteIv only exercises wrong-length, not the null-IV branch
findings.description: TokenEncryptor.decrypt guards both `iv == null || iv.length != IV_BYTES`. The test passes a 16-byte zero IV, so the length branch is covered but the null branch is not. Removing the `iv == null ||` short-circuit from production would not make this test fail, so the litmus test is partially weak for that line.
findings.suggestion: Either add a parameterized case `decryptRejectsNullIv` that calls `encryptor.decrypt(null, anyCiphertext)` and asserts `IllegalArgumentException` with a message containing 'null', or convert the existing test to a JUnit `@ParameterizedTest` over `{null, new byte[0], new byte[11], new byte[16]}` to cover all rejected shapes in one place.

findings.title: Boot-validation test asserts via stack-trace substring on the class simple name
findings.description: The three failure-path tests assert with `.hasStackTraceContaining("IllegalStateException")`. That string match is satisfied by any IllegalStateException anywhere in the chain (including the future addition of an unrelated IllegalStateException further up the Spring stack) and would silently break if someone renames the wrapper or wraps the cause in a different exception type. The accompanying comment correctly explains why `.rootCause()` cannot be used (the chained NumberFormatException sits below ours), but a structural walk would be stronger than a textual one.
findings.suggestion: Replace the textual match with a small helper that walks `Throwable.getCause()` and finds the first IllegalStateException, then assert on its message: `assertThat(findInCauseChain(context.getStartupFailure(), IllegalStateException.class)).isPresent().get().extracting(Throwable::getMessage).asString().contains("BOT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY");`. Keeps the same behavioral guarantee but is refactor-safe.

findings.title: tamperedIvRejected contains a defensive collision guard that is effectively dead code
findings.description: Lines 78-80 check `if (Arrays.equals(otherIv, encrypted.iv()))` and XOR the first byte if so. The probability of a 12-byte SecureRandom collision is 2^-96 — astronomically lower than the test infrastructure failing for unrelated reasons. The branch is never exercised, adds visual noise, and slightly obscures the intent of the test.
findings.suggestion: Drop the conditional and just XOR a byte of the encrypted IV unconditionally to derive otherIv: `byte[] otherIv = encrypted.iv().clone(); otherIv[0] ^= 0x01;`. This makes the diff from the valid IV explicit (one bit), removes the conditional, and removes the SecureRandom dependency from this particular test.

findings.title: missingKeyFailsFast does not cover the null-key path through the constructor
findings.description: decodeKey guards `hexKey == null || hexKey.isBlank()`. Production cannot reach the null branch via `@Value` (Spring substitutes empty string for `${prop:}`), so this is not a real defect. But the test only exercises the blank-string branch, so removing the `hexKey == null ||` short-circuit from production would not make any test fail.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line parameterized case feeding both `""` and `null` through `new TokenEncryptor(...)` and asserting the same IllegalStateException. Two seconds of test code, locks in the contract that the constructor is null-safe even if a future caller invokes it directly.
